newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close higher, further rise seen.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close higher, further rise seen.

text.p: Stocks ended higher on Saturday after fluctuating widely as early gains were eroded by late profit-taking, brokers said.
Ample liquidity would push the market higher early next week with the index testing 750-770, they said.
The composite index closed 1.32 points higher at 722.32.

"Overall sentiment was buoyed by abundant money supply. But there seem to be a lot of stocks to be sold at around 720," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities. Brokers said customer deposits with brokerage firms were estimated at more than three trillion won, up from 2.95 trillion last week.
Brokers said institutions, encouraged by the market's firm rises over a period, would include blue chips in their portfolios next week.
The defection of a high-ranking North Korean official and the Hanbo scandal were ignored as factors.
"I would see the index rising to 750-770 by the middle of next week," said Yoo Hae-kyong of Daishin Securities.
Volume totalled 27.11 million shares for Saturday's half-day trading compared with 39.07 million on Friday. Gainers outpaced losers 375 to 361 with 171 unchanged.
